solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pig-tail included in feature on coiffure

indicators.note: included in tells us the pig's tail letter goes inside the facial feature

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
the tail, or last letter, of the word pig is G
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pigtail tucked into a hairstyle, as a stylist might describe it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chignon is a knot or roll of hair worn at the nape, a kind of hairdo.

clue.text: Tragic ending — as in De Niro's last film

indicators.note: ending asks for the final letter of the word tragic

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the actor's name De Niro

explanation.surface: A tragic finale, just as in the last movie Robert De Niro made.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1995 Scorsese picture starring De Niro has this very title, so the surface is almost a definition in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Casino is the title of a 1995 Martin Scorsese movie starring Robert De Niro.

clue.text: Dye of a kind I got from woad

indicators.note: of signals that the letters come from within the run kind I got

explanation.surface: A dye of some sort that I obtained from the woad plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: woad was the old European source of this blue dye, so the last words add colour rather than wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue dye, once got in Europe from woad.

clue.text: Bar, of course, two prominent extractions, canine teeth have new filling and cavity

indicators.note: filling means a letter is packed into the remaining teeth
the two most prominent, leading, letters are pulled out of canine teeth

parts.note: a cavity is a hole

explanation.surface: A dental tale: two front teeth pulled, the canines filled, and a cavity found.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing C and A from CANINE TEETH leaves NINETEETH; N goes in before the TH. 'Of course' means at a golf course: the bar after the eighteenth.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers jokingly call the clubhouse bar the extra hole played after the eighteenth on a course.

clue.text: What was heard of Shergar in 1982

definitions.text: What was heard of Shergar in 1982

parts.words: What was heard of Shergar in 1982
parts.note: Shergar, a famous Derby-winning racehorse, was kidnapped in 1983 and never seen again, so in 1982 he could still make a horse's cry

explanation.surface: A question about news of the racehorse Shergar in 1982.
explanation.walkthrough: Shergar, the 1981 Derby winner, was stolen from an Irish stud in February 1983 and never found, so 'what was heard of him' sounds like a question about news.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry a horse makes, so it is the sound Shergar made while still around.

clue.text: Seaside location report of scandal involving BBC man

indicators.note: report of means we want the sound of the phrase, not its spelling

parts.note: a scandal gets the suffix -gate, and the BBC man is presenter Andrew Marr, so a Marr scandal is Marrgate

explanation.surface: A news report of a scandal at a resort involving a BBC presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Marr is a long-serving BBC political presenter; any scandal is dubbed '-gate' after Watergate. MARGATE is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a traditional English seaside resort town on the Kent coast.

clue.text: Style associated with kind of bag or chair

parts.note: mode is a fashion or style
a ratbag is a British insult, so rat is the kind of bag
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion linked to a type of handbag or a chair design.
explanation.walkthrough: RATBAG is British slang for a nasty person; here only its first part, RAT, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a debate is to preside over it, which is the job of a moderator.

clue.text: Tableware it can be beneficial to break

definitions.meaning: a knife ... is a small piece of tableware for propping cutlery

definitions.text: it can be beneficial to break
definitions.meaning: a short pause from work, a break, can do you good

explanation.surface: Crockery that, oddly, is better broken.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests smashing plates; the second sense is a pause that is beneficial when you take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest is both a cutlery stand on the table and a break from activity.

clue.text: A game with intermittently daring revolutionary defence

parts.note: taken as written
polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: revolutionary turns the picked letters round
intermittently takes every other letter of daring

explanation.surface: A game played with occasional daring by a revolutionary defender.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of dArInG give AIG, which 'revolutionary' turns to GIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence or justification of one's beliefs or conduct.

clue.text: Vide Matthew 20:6 or 23:59

definitions.meaning: in the parable of the vineyard labourers
one minute before midnight is the last possible moment

explanation.surface: A footnote referring the reader to a Bible verse or to a clock time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vide' is Latin for 'see', used in references. The parable says labourers were hired at the eleventh hour of the working day.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the last moment, and comes from the Gospel parable of workers hired late.

clue.text: Litter rarely picked up these days in saloon

definitions.text: Litter rarely picked up these days
definitions.meaning: a litter is a carried chair, and the ... chair is seldom lifted by bearers now
a saloon is the British name for a closed car with a boot

explanation.surface: Rubbish that is seldom picked up nowadays in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Litter here is a carried seat, not rubbish; 'picked up' means lifted by bearers. A saloon is British for a four-door car, called a sedan in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan is a carried chair for one passenger and also the American word for a saloon car.

clue.text: Make unsuitable kind of music without Portishead's leaders on board

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places the music around the rest

parts.note: indie is a genre of alternative rock music

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts the letters within SS

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel you are on board
the leading letters of the band name Portishead are P and O

explanation.surface: A music genre gets spoiled when the band Portishead's frontmen are absent from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Portishead is a Bristol trip-hop band. 'On board' is the usual crossword signal for going inside the steamship abbreviation, and 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To indispose someone is to render them unfit or unwilling for something.

clue.text: One garment on top of another

definitions.text: One garment on top of another

parts.words: One garment on top of another
parts.note: the second element of the word is itself a garment, a shirt, sitting after a word for the dark hours

explanation.surface: Layering clothes, one on top of the next.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests layering clothes; the garment is one worn in bed, which can go over other bedwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightshirt is a long loose shirt worn as bedwear, a garment in its own right.

clue.text: See 3
In-store surveillance expert?

parts.note: a shop detective might lurk by the shop counter, but the real sense is an agent working against enemy spies

explanation.surface: A question about who watches shoplifters in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a store detective behind the counter; the real meaning is an agent in counter-espionage.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterspy is an agent who works against enemy espionage.

clue.text: Someone with welcome employment working in esoteric physical therapy

indicators.note: working signals that the letters are reshaped into something else

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation for physical training or therapy

explanation.surface: A practitioner of an obscure form of physiotherapy describes the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' is the anagram signal over IN, ESOTERIC and PT.
explanation.definitionFit: A front-desk worker greets visitors, so the job literally consists of welcoming people.

clue.text: Old, old party appearing before end of dinner is head maid collecting plates

parts.note: ex- means former, old
Lib is short for the old Liberal Party

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of dinner

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of maid

explanation.surface: An elderly guest at an old party arrives before the end of dinner, while the head maid gathers up the plates.
explanation.walkthrough: The plates are bookplates, labels pasted into books, not dinner plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Exlibrism is the hobby of collecting bookplates, labels marked ex libris.

clue.text: Temper made lout troublesome

indicators.note: troublesome suggests disorder, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A loutish youth's behaviour put someone in a bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun for anger but is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to moderate or adjust it, which is what modulate means.

clue.text: Don's heartless executioner behind abominable unending cruelty

indicators.note: behind places the next piece after the jumble
abominable suggests something twisted, so the letters are reordered
unending removes the final letter of cruelty
heartless strips the middle out, keeping only the outer letters of executioner

explanation.surface: A heartless executioner carries out unspeakable cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don's' is read as 'don is', a don being an Oxbridge academic; 'abominable' rearranges the cruelty letters, not describing the executioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher at Oxford or Cambridge, a type of academic teacher.

clue.text: Conspicuous 'Bravo!' precedes diatribe that's too mealy-mouthed

parts.note: overt means open, plainly visible
ole is a cry of approval like bravo
a rant is a bitter tirade

explanation.surface: A loud cheer comes before a tirade, which seems too timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precedes' simply puts the cheer before the rant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too mealy-mouthed avoids frank criticism, which is excessively forgiving and indulgent.

clue.text: Look over outskirts of Bilbao to belvedere

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above the following piece

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: outskirts of picks the first and last letters of Bilbao

explanation.surface: A visitor looks over the edges of Bilbao from a viewpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: A belvedere is a building placed to command a fine view.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a garden summerhouse with an open view, a type of belvedere.

clue.text: Tamper with resonance of gong

indicators.note: resonance of means the sound of a word is wanted

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: Interfering with the sound a gong makes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a gong is a medal or honour, not only a struck metal disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere or tamper with something.

clue.text: Educated at university, then Telegraph office over seas

parts.note: being up means in residence at university
TO is the abbreviation for telegraph office

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: the deeps are the seas

explanation.surface: After university the graduate went to work at the Telegraph newspaper's overseas office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns DEEPS round; 'overseas' in the surface is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well informed and current with knowledge is the same as being educated in a subject.

clue.text: Loiter and abet criminal in black out

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspect hangs around and helps a criminal in a blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' is the anagram signal over LOITER and ABET.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to erase or blot out completely, as when text is blacked out.

clue.text: Leading scientist withdraws from backing breakfast cereal as 'essential aid to digestion'

indicators.note: withdraws from removes a letter from the reversed cereal
backing means the cereal is written backwards

parts.note: muesli is a breakfast cereal of oats and dried fruit

indicators.note: leading gives the first letter of scientist

explanation.surface: A top scientist withdraws support for a breakfast cereal advertised as essential for digestion.
explanation.walkthrough: MUESLI turned round is ILSEUM; taking out S leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final part of the small intestine, where much nutrient absorption happens.

clue.text: See 8
Biggles' band missing special song by Sting among others

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
Sting was lead singer of the band The Police

explanation.surface: A Biggles group lacking a special number accompanied by the singer Sting and others.
explanation.walkthrough: W.E. Johns's air ace Biggles served in the Special Air Police; drop 'special' and you have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggles of the Special Air Police is a book title; without the first word, that unit remains.

clue.text: See 21
Listened in London to singular tympanum

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner drops the initial aitch

parts.note: heard means listened to
rum is British slang for odd or singular

explanation.surface: Someone listened in London to a singular performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops initial H, so HEARD becomes 'EARD. Singular here means strange, which RUM means in old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanum is the membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, the eardrum.

clue.text: Seasonal staff employ a drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Seasonal workers hire someone who is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasonal staff' sounds like temporary workers, but staff is a pole raised for May Day.
explanation.definitionFit: A maypole is a tall pole, or staff, decorated for May Day festivities each spring.
